samples.summary: Shipped user guide still documents API keys as owner-only and describes the now-removed UI gate
samples.evidence: The change opens minting/listing/revoking to any member and removes the `isOwner` gate on the Settings API Keys section, and it updated docs/design/*.md and packages/backend/README.md. But the end-user documentation package was missed: `guide/workspaces.md:42-43` still says "Create or revoke an API key | No | Yes" and "See the list of API keys | Yes, but only via the CLI or REST API"; line 87 lists "**API Keys** — *owners only*"; line 90 says "A member sees the first three sections and nothing below them"; and the tip at lines 92-97 states "creating and revoking are owner-only. The Settings page … hides the whole **API Keys** section from anyone who isn't an owner … There is nothing to find in Settings." All of these are now false, and this is the page members actually read to learn whether they can mint a key.

samples.summary: Design-sandbox API key fixture not updated with the new `createdBy` field the owner-only column reads
samples.evidence: `FIXTURE_API_KEYS` entries carry only id/name/prefix/createdAt/lastUsedAt, while the new owner-only "Created by" column calls `creatorName(apiKey.createdBy)` (workspace-settings.tsx:153). In the workspace-settings visual scene the column will render "Unknown" for every row, so the new UI is not actually exercised by the sandbox/visual lane.
searchedFor: grep createdBy in packages/frontend and packages/design-sandbox

samples.summary: Developer REST docs still describe an API key's authority as the workspace's, not its minter's
samples.evidence: The authority table says an API key's authority is "The workspace the key was minted for, plus the key's `scopes`". With minting now open to every member, the distinction the design docs make in this change — a key carries *its minter's* membership resolved per request — is exactly what a reader of this page needs and is absent here. Pre-existing text, but this change is what makes it materially misleading.

samples.summary: CLI schema for `api-keys.list` does not declare the new `createdBy` field
samples.evidence: `response: { type: 'array', items: { id, name, prefix } }` — the list endpoint now also returns `createdBy`, which is the field that distinguishes keys in an owner's workspace-wide listing. Harmless if the schema is documentation-only, but it is the CLI's stated contract and the diff extended the payload without touching it.

finding.summary: Shipped user guide still documents API keys as owner-only and describes the now-removed UI gate
finding.evidence: The change opens minting/listing/revoking to any member and removes the `isOwner` gate on the Settings API Keys section, and it updated docs/design/*.md and packages/backend/README.md. But the end-user documentation package was missed: `guide/workspaces.md:42-43` still says "Create or revoke an API key | No | Yes" and "See the list of API keys | Yes, but only via the CLI or REST API"; line 87 lists "**API Keys** — *owners only*"; line 90 says "A member sees the first three sections and nothing below them"; and the tip at lines 92-97 states "creating and revoking are owner-only. verdict.reason: Every quoted string is present verbatim in packages/documentation/guide/workspaces.md (L42-43 permission table rows, L87 "API Keys — owners only", L90 "first three sections and nothing below them", L92-97 tip claiming Settings hides the section). All are now false: workspace-settings.tsx:432-505 renders the API Keys section and its Separator unconditionally (isOwner survives only for the "Created by" column at L460/473 and the description text at L439-441, while Danger Zone at L508 stays gated), and api-key.controller.ts:47/64/76/87-88 uses assertMember/keyScope instead of assertOwner for create, list, and revoke. The page is shipped end-user documentation, linked in the published VitePress sidebar at packages/documentation/.vitepress/config.ts:87. The change's own task file (docs/tasks/active/20260913-member-api-keys-todo.md:47,50) confirms the frontend gate was dropped and that the Docs task covered only packages/backend/README.md and docs/design/rest-api.md, with the later review listing five further doc sites fixed — none in packages/documentation. No guard or caller makes the stale text unreachable. Cost falls outside codebase tidiness: the page a member reads to learn whether they can mint a key affirmatively tells them "No" and that Settings has nothing to show, so the issue's outcome does not reach the user on the surface documented for it.
